summary:
Held 1 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 5 upside misses — COHR +9%, ON +7%, GLW +7%, VRT +6%, CIEN +6%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (PLTR -7%, ACN -7%, GEN -6%, NFLX -6%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: COHR (+9.11%) — BofA raised its 2030 AI datacenter TAM estimate to ~$1.7T (from ~$1.4T), lifting optical stocks broadly; compounded by JPMorgan Overweight reaffirm and CMB International $465 street-high Buy initiation the prior session. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — COHR is a large-cap AI photonics/optical-networking name likely excluded by sector or industry filter. Move was day 2 of a back-to-back analyst/sector-upgrade cascade (+11.3% Jun 22 then +9.1% Jun 23); pre-open positioning was the only viable entry.

top_movers.catalyst: GF Securities upgraded SMCI to Buy with a $48 target and Supermicro unveiled a Vera Rubin NVL4 data center blueprint at ISC 2026 in Hamburg, the twin catalysts driving the +16% rally.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SMCI was likely on a compliance exclusion list stemming from 2024-25 late-filing and auditor-change issues. News-reactive-disclosure flagged the events but could not act without explicit universe membership.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-compliance-clearance gate to news-reactive-disclosure: names exiting the exclusion list become intraday-eligible on the next analyst upgrade ≥2 notches, capped at 0.5% gross exposure until two clean annual filings are on record.

top_movers.suggestion: Add a SOX-momentum gate: when the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gains >2% intraday on a named NVIDIA/AI hardware catalyst, auto-scan AI-supply-chain names with AI-datacenter revenue exposure (e.g. ON, MPWR) for a 1-hour momentum entry with a 3% hard stop.

top_movers.catalyst: CIEN fell 15% on June 4 despite Q2 EPS beat ($1.64 vs $1.46 est) and raised FY guidance to $6.3B; stock recovering aided by AI optical networking sector tailwinds and broad analyst price target upgrades.

top_movers.suggestion: Add a sovereign-contract-cancellation news trigger: flag affected tickers for exit/avoid within 1 session of any G7 government announcing a US-tech vendor replacement, preventing being caught long in multi-day government-contract unwinds.

top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings continuation rule: names with an initial gap ≤–10% on earnings day that close lower for 2 consecutive sessions become eligible short candidates on day-3 open, gated by ADV ≥ $300M to cover large-caps like ACN.

top_movers.catalyst: Nasdaq sell-off (-1.32%) driven by South Korean memory-ETF regulator warning; IBM+OpenAI enterprise cybersecurity AI partnership announced same day amplified the drop for consumer security incumbent GEN.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe; GEN (~$14B, Norton/LifeLock consumer security) sits outside enterprise-tech momentum scope. Move was macro sell-off plus competitive narrative fear, not a pre-positionable company-specific catalyst.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change — the sell-off reflects macro rotation and AI-disruption narrative requiring short capability not currently in scope; adding long exposure on a -6% day would run counter to risk parameters.
